newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares sail to ninth straight record high.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares sail to ninth straight record high.

text.p: Egyptian share prices hopped 0.6 percent to a ninth record high on Wednesday, adding to a 24 percent jump from their levels at the beginning of the year.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) all-share index rose 2.32 points from Tuesday to close at 369.89 points.
Turnover was an average 53.89 million pounds ($15.85 million) with investors focusing mainly on giant realestate firm Medinet Nasr and Development and the popular milling and cement sectors.
Medinet Nasr was the most active share for the second day in a row, rising 6.0 pounds to 471 on turnover of 12.9 million pounds.
Amriyah Cement came second, trading shares worth 6.3 million and closing 0.84 pounds higher at 84.25.
Helwan Portland Cement performed even better and rose 1.00 to 80.8. Suez Cement gained 0.2 to 72.
The flour millers, all of them former state companies which have been privatised, also helped take the market higher.
North Cairo Flour Mills shot up 8.75 pounds to a new record high of 187.25. The stock closed at an all-time high of 178.50 pounds on Tuesday.
Central and West Delta Flour Mills added to week-long gains and closed 5.43 pounds higher at 113.94 and Upper Egypt Flour Mills also rose 2.81 to 89.21.
The index for openly traded firms rose to 604.02 points from 600.34 points on Tuesday and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms also gained 1.58 points to 245.67.
Out of the 76 shares traded, 42 gained, 14 lost and 20 ended the day unchanged.
